definition: prefix placed before a verb, number or describing word to make a noun phrase, as in {a masa}, the first, {a nihna}, the second, and {a thatpa}, the one who kills
particle prefixed to form verb past tense

third person marker placed before a noun to show the possessor, as in {a pawlpihte}, its allies, and {a genna}, his statement; the prefix {a} of the other senses stands before a verb or describing word
placed after a pronoun or noun for the owner, the thing owned being left out: <kei a> is mine, <mikangte-a> that of the English
placed after the verb of a clause, joins it to the clause that follows, as in {Vasa leeng a, ngasa in tui peek hi}, birds fly and fish swim
placed after a pronoun it makes the possessive pronoun, the thing owned by that person: <kei a> is mine, <nang a> yours, <ei a> ours, <amau a> theirs
the third person marker <a> written with a capital at the start of a sentence or quoted line; before a noun it shows the possessor, his, her, its or their, and before a verb it marks the subject

the prefix <a> written with a capital at the start of a sentence, before a describing word or a noun made from a verb, as in {A nung ciangin}, afterwards, {A mawkna-in}, in vain, and {A beina}, the end
the time gone by, and in grammar the past tense, which the book makes with <khin> after the verb, as in {ka paikhin hi}, I went; the lexicon also has the spelling <abeisa hun>
the past perfect continuous tense, made by saying the verb twice before <khinzota>, as in {zatui kei hong na piapia khinzota hi}, she had been giving me medicine

the past continuous tense, made with the verb form in <khit> followed by <laitak>, as in {sum a piakkhit laitak ahi hi}, they were giving money

<ahat> and <luat> written as one word: when it is too strong or too fast, said of wind and of a train
<a> and <hatna> written as one word: the strength, force or speed of something, as of a wind, an earthquake or a vehicle
<a> and <hatpen>, strongest, written as one word: the strongest one, that is the strongest
<a> and <hatsakna> written as one word: the thing that makes it go fast, said of the accelerator pedal of a car and followed by the English word Accelerator
<ahat> and <tai> written as one word, of a vehicle: that runs fast, going at high speed
<hau>, rich, with the prefix <a> written joined: the rich; {ahau azawng} is rich and poor alike
<a> and <hauh> written as one word: he is or becomes rich, his being rich; {ahauh nading} is so that he may become rich
<a> and <hauhna>, wealth, written as one word: his, her, its or their wealth, how rich someone is
<a> and <haupen>, richest, written as one word: the richest one
<a> and <haute> written as one word: those who are rich; after a noun, those who have much of it
<a> and <hauzaw> written as one word: richer, the one who is richer; after <sangin> richer than
place in Babylonia and the canal named after it, where Ezra gathered the exiles before the journey to Jerusalem
<a> and <hawh> written as one word: he or she visits, the one who visits; {ahawh laitak} is while visiting
<a>, <hawh> and <ding> written as one word: that he or she will visit, most often with <in>, in order to visit a place or a person
<a> with <hawh> and <pak> written as one word: he or she is there on a short visit, the one who is visiting for a while and does not live there
<a>, <hawh> and <sung> written as one word: during the time that someone is visiting a place
<a> with <hawih>, another spelling of <hoih>, good, written as one word: it is good, the good one; {ahawih leh asia} is the good and the bad
<a> and <hawl>, drive, written as one word: he drives, the one who drives, the vehicle that someone drives

terms: who is to drive/who will drive
definition: <a> and <hawlding> written as one word: the one who is to drive a vehicle or fly an aircraft
<a> and <hawlgawp> written as one word: he drove fast and without care
<ahawl> and <kawm>, while, written as one word: while he or she is driving, usually followed by <in>
<a> and <hawlkhia> written as one word: he drives someone out or expels him; also of a vehicle, he drives it away
<a> and <hawlkhiat>, drive out, written as one word: that he or they drive out or expel; also of driving a vehicle away
<ahawl> and <laitak> written as one word: at the very time when he or she was driving
<a> and <hawlna> written as one word: the part from which a vehicle is driven, its steering, handlebars or driver's cab
<a> and <hawlna> written as one word: the fact or manner of someone driving
<a> and <hawlnu> written as one word: the woman who was driving it
<a> and <hawlpa> written as one word: the man who drives the vehicle or flies the aircraft just named
<a>, <hawl>, drive, and <pen> written as one word: the one who was driving the vehicle, as the topic of the sentence
<ahawl>, the one that drives, with the ending {-pi}, great: the chief force or party that moves a matter forward
<a> and <hawlte> written as one word: the one or ones who drive the vehicle; said also of a single driver, as in {mawtaw ahawlte tutna}, the driver's seat
<a> and <hawm>, divide, written as one word: he or it distributes, shares out
<a> and <hawm>, empty, written as one word: empty, with nothing or nobody inside, or the empty one
<ahawm>, distribute, and <ding> written as one word: that he will hand out, in order to distribute money, aid or papers
<a> and <hawmkhia> written as one word: he or they distribute something, or the one who distributes it
<a> and <hawmkhiat> written as one word: he or they distribute or hand out something; also of a supplier of goods and of an artist who releases an album
<a> and <hawng> written as one word: the outer covering of something, as the peel of a fruit, a husk, or the casing of a bullet
king of Judah, son of Jotham and father of Hezekiah
name of two kings, the son of Ahab who ruled Israel and the son of Jehoram who ruled Judah
<Ahaziah> with the plural ending <te>, Ahaziah and the kings named with him
son of Abishur and Abihail, of the tribe of Judah
<ah>, in or at, with the particle <bel>, written as one word: marks a place or matter that is set against others, as for in; {Zogam ahbel} is in Zogam, for its part
<a> and <heh> written as one word: he, she or they are angry, or the one who is angry; {aheh suak} is become furious
<a> and <hehna>, anger, written as one word: his, her or, with <uh>, their anger
<a> and <hehpih> written as one word: he pities, or the one who pities; {ahehpih huai} is pitiable
<a> and <hehpihhuai>, pitiable, written as one word: who is to be pitied; {ahehpihhuai mahmah} is very pitiable
<a> and <hehsuak> written as one word: he or she became angry, or the one who became angry
<ahehsuak> and <lua> written as one word: he or she became very angry, too angry
<a> and <hel>, mix, written as one word: he or they mix something in, what is mixed in, the one who mixes
<hem>, deformed, with the prefix <a> written joined: one that is maimed; said of an animal unfit for offering
<a> and <hepkhiat> written as one word: he removes, they took away, what was removed
word indicating nominative case
<a> with <hi>: it is, it is so, the affirmative that <ahilo> denies; <ahi laigual> is a positive sentence
son of Abdiel, head of a family of the tribe of Gad
<ahi>, is, written in capital letters in an inscription or a name that is set in capitals
a sentence that states that something is so and contains none of the negative words <lo>, <kei> or <keng>
a sentence that states that something is not so and contains one of the negative words <lo>, <kei> or <keng>
sentence final denoting interrogation or exclamation
one of the leaders who sealed the covenant in the time of Nehemiah
sentence final denoting interrogation or exclamation
son of Sharar the Hararite, one of the mighty men of David
<a> and <hiamtawi> written as one word: the weapon that someone carries
son of Shemida, of the tribe of Manasseh
<a>, its, and <hiang>, branch, written as one word: the branches of a tree, and also the branches of an organisation

terms: as it is/like this/in this way
definition: <a> and <hici>, like this, written as one word: in the same way as before, as it stands

terms: to some extent/to a certain degree
definition: <ahi> and <ciangkhat> written as one word: up to a certain point, to some extent
<ahi>, it is, and the question word <diam> written as one word: closes a question or a doubt, is it so, could it be that
<a>, <hi> and <ding> written as one word: what is to be or ought to be; {ahiding mah} is just as it should be, and {ahiding in ummawh} is suspect that it is
son of Ammishaddai, leader of the tribe of Dan in the wilderness
<a> with <hih>, the form of <hi>, be, used before <ciangin>, <leh>, <manin> and <hangin>: it being so, this having happened
<ahih>, being so, with <hangin>, although: although that is so; joins two statements that contrast

<ahih>, being so, and <mahbangin>, just as: placed after a noun phrase or clause, as befits one who is that, since it is so; {tua ahih mahbangin} at the head of a sentence is accordingly, that being so
<ahih>, be so, and <manun>, because, the form used when the subject is plural: placed at the end of the clause that gives the reason, because they are or because they do

terms: whenever it is/as long as it is/when it comes to
definition: <ahih>, being so, and <nakleh>, as long as: placed after a noun or a clause, whenever it is that, provided that it is so
<ahih>, its being so, and <zahkhat>, to the same degree: followed by <in>, it closes a first clause, just as this is so, and the main clause then states what holds equally or on the other hand
<ahih>, being so, <zahkhat>, to the same degree, and <in>: placed at the end of a first clause, it sets that statement beside the next one as equally true, just as the one is so, the other is so too
<ahih> and <ciang> written as one word, a short form of <ahihciangin>: placed at the end of a clause, since that is so
<ahih> and <cianga> written as one word after a clause: that being so, because of that
{ahih ciangin} written as one word; {tua ahihciangin} is that being so, therefore
<ahih>, being so, and <ding>, will, written as one word: that it will be, that it should be, or that it may be; with <kisam> it is required to be, and with <patau> or <lamen> feared or hoped to be
<ahi>, it is, and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word: closes a statement that says what something is
<ahi> and <hiam> written as one word at the end of a question: is it so, and after <bang> what is it
short form of {ahih kei leh}, if it is not so: or, joining two words or clauses as alternatives
<ahih> and <kei>, not, written as one word, nearly always followed by <leh>: if it is not so, or else, or
<ahih>, <kei> and <leh> written as one word, if it is not so: between two words it means or, and at the start of a clause otherwise
<a> with <hih>, the form of <hi>, be, used before a suffix, and <khak>, happen to; {ahihkhak leh} is if it should be so
{a hih lam} written as one word, the fact of being so, mostly before <thei>, <phawk> or <mu>: know, realize or see that it is
<ahihlam>, that it is so, and <phawk>, remember: closes a clause and tells the reader to keep in mind what the clause says; followed by <in>, <ni> or <hen>, often with <gige>, always

terms: even that it is/also that it was
definition: <ahihlam> and <zong> written as one word, before a verb of knowing or noticing: even the fact that it is so
<ahih>, being so, with <leh>, if: if it is, if he is, after a noun or a clause
particle comparison between verbs to delineate their relationship
<hihloh>, not being, with the prefix <a> written as one word; {ahihleh ahihloh} is whether it is so or not, and <ahihloh hangin> is although it is not
<ahihloh>, not being, and <hangin>, here although and not because: placed after a noun or a describing word at the end of a clause, although it is not that; the negative of <ahih hangin>

terms: that it is not/that he is not
definition: <ahihloh>, not be, and <lam>, the fact that, written as one word, mostly before <thei> or <kilang>: the fact that it is not so
<ahihloh>, not being, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact that something is not so, used where English says that it is not
<ahih>, being, and <ma>, before, written as one word: before someone is or becomes what the word before it names; also written {a hihma}

terms: since it is/as it really is
definition: <ahih> and <mah> written as one word, followed by <bangin>: just as it is, since it really is so

terms: as it is/since it is/just as
definition: <ahihmah>, it really is, and <bangin>, like: placed after a noun or a clause, since it is that, in keeping with its being so. What follows is what one would expect from this, and often takes up the same thought with <zong>, also
<ahih>, being so, and the first part of <manin> written as one word, with <in> written apart: because it is so; {tua ahihman in} is therefore
<ahih> and <manin> written as one word: because it is so; <tua ahihmanin> is therefore
the fact that something is so; placed after a clause that is the object of a verb of knowing, seeing or showing, where English says that
in grammar, the plain form of a describing word, as <hoih>, good, set beside the comparative with <zaw> and the superlative with <pen>; the book heads the column {Ahihna} and glosses it positive

terms: it is evident that/it is clear that
definition: <ahihna>, the fact of being so, and <kilang>, appear: closes a clause and states that what the clause says is shown to be true; often followed by <mahmah> and <hi>

terms: it is seen that/it is evident that
definition: <ahihna>, the fact that it is so, and <kimu>, here be seen and not meet: placed after a clause, it is seen that this is so; mostly {ahihna kimu thei hi}, it can be seen that, closing a conclusion drawn from what was said

terms: the fact that/that it is so
definition: <ahihna>, its being so, and <thu>, matter: placed after a clause and before a verb of saying or announcing such as <gen> or <pulak>, it turns the clause into what is said, where English says that

terms: if it is/as for/when it comes to
definition: <ahih>, being so, written together with the first part of <nakleh>, if: {ahihnak leh} is if it is, as long as it is, and after a noun as for, when it comes to

terms: if it is/as long as it is/provided that it is
definition: <ahih>, being so, and <nakleh>, if indeed, written as one word: if it really is, as long as it is

terms: even if it is/though it be
definition: <ahih> and <phial> written as one word; followed by <lehzong> it means even if it really is so
<ahih> it being so and <tawh> with, written as one word after a clause: since it is, with its being so, and for that reason
The verb <hih>, do, with the prefix <a> and the plural <te>: the people who do the thing named before it, as in {mawhna ahihte}, those who sin.
<ahih>, it being so, and <teh> written as one word at the end of a clause: since that is so, giving the reason for what follows; {tua ahihteh} is that being so
<a> and <hihtheih> written as one word: what can be done; {ahihtheih leh} is if possible, and {ahihtheih bangin} or {ahihtheih zahin} is as far as possible
<ahihtheih> and <leh> written as one word: if it can be done, if possible
spelling of Ahihud in 1 Chronicles 8.7, a man of the tribe of Benjamin
name of two men: a leader of the tribe of Asher, son of Shelomi, who helped divide the land, and a man of Benjamin

terms: as much as it is/to the same degree
definition: <ahih>, its being so, and <zah>, amount, written as one word and followed by <khatin>: in the same measure as something is so
<ahih>, being, and <zawh>, after or since, written as one word: since he became that; in one sentence it is rather <zawh>, be able, with <nading>: so that it can become

terms: the way it is/the fact that it is
definition: <ahih>, it being so, and <zia>, manner, written as one word, placed after a description: how or that someone or something is so, as in {manpha ahihzia}, how precious it is
<ahih> and <zong> written as one word and followed by <in> at the start of a sentence: although that is so, but; the same as <ahizongin>
name of several men, among them a priest in the time of Saul, the prophet of Shiloh, and one of David's warriors
son of Shaphan, an official of King Josiah who protected Jeremiah, and father of Gedaliah
short spoken form of {ahih kei leh}, if it is not so: joins two alternatives, or opens a sentence with otherwise
<a> and <hikei>, is not, written as one word: it is not, that which is not; {ahikei-zong} is although it is not
<ahi>, it is, and <khadiam> written as one word at the end of a clause: might it be, I wonder whether it is, said of a guess or suspicion
<a>, <hi> and <lam> written as one word: that something is so, the fact of its being so, as the object of a verb such as <phawk>, remember
<a> and <hilel>, be merely, written as one word: it is nothing more than that
The verb <hilh>, teach, written together with the preceding <a>, the third person marker; it is usually written {a hilh}.
<a> and <hilo>, is not, written as one word: that is not, what is not; {ahi le ahilo} is whether it is so or not
<a> and <hilopi>, though not so, written as one word: what is not really so, a thing that is not the real one
<ahilo>, is not, with the plural <te>, written as one word after a noun: those who are not that, as in {Christian ahilote}, non-Christians
father of Jehoshaphat, the recorder of David and Solomon
name of several men, among them the son of Zadok the priest, and a son-in-law of Solomon who was governor in Naphtali
spelling of Ahimaaz in 2 Samuel 18.22, the son of Zadok the priest who ran with news to David
name of several men, among them the son of Zadok the priest, and a son-in-law of Solomon who was governor in Naphtali
<ahi> and <mah> written as one word: it is indeed so; in a question, is it really so
name of two men: one of the three sons of Anak driven out of Hebron by Caleb, and a Levite gatekeeper
<ahih> and <manin> written as one word and without the h: because it is so; {tua ahimanin} is therefore
<ahi>, it is, and the exclaiming <maw>, written as one word at the end of a statement: it is so, you know; said of what the speaker asserts or quotes
name of two priests: the priest at Nob who helped David and was killed by Saul, and a son of Abiathar
Levite of the line of Kohath, a son of Elkanah
son of Iddo, one of Solomon's twelve district governors, at Mahanaim
<ahi>, it is, with <nak>, followed by <leh>, if: {ahinak leh}, if it really is so; listed by the book among the conjunctions
The word <hing>, alive, with the prefix <a> written as one word: who is alive, that lives; {ahing tawntung} is living or lasting for ever.
<a> and <hingin> written as one word: alive, while still living, said of a person or animal that is caught, found or rescued
<a> and <hinglai> written as one word: one that is still alive, while still alive
<ahing>, alive, with an ending that tells the state someone is in; with <in>, {ahingtang in} tells that something is done to a person or animal that is still alive, as buried alive or burnt alive
<ahing>, alive, with <tangpi> written as one word: while still living, said of one who is buried, burned or thrown to animals alive
name of two women: a wife of David from Jezreel, the mother of Amnon, and the wife of Saul
name of several men, among them the son of Abinadab who walked in front of the cart carrying the ark

terms: the one who is/he who is
definition: The verb <ahi>, is, with <pa>, the male one: it closes a describing phrase and is said of God, as in {Pasian ahipa}, the one who is God.
<a> and <hipah>, be at once, written as one word: it is thereby also so, it is outright so; {ahipah kei zongin} is even if it is not exactly so
<ahi>, be, with <phial>, even if, written as one word and followed by <zongin> or {zong in}: even if it is, even if it were
<ahiphial>, even if it is, and <zongin>, although: placed after a noun, a describing word or a clause, even if it is so, even though that is the case; the main statement follows
son of Enan, leader of the tribe of Naphtali in the wilderness
son of Benjamin, ancestor of the Ahiramite clan
<a>, <hi>, be, and <sa>, here already, written as one word: that already is so, placed after the thing it describes; {US Gammi ahisa khat} is one who is already a citizen of the United States
man of the tribe of Dan, father of the craftsman Oholiab
official in charge of Solomon's palace; in 1 Chronicles 7.10 the name stands for Ahishahar, a man of Benjamin
The verb <ahi>, be, with <ta>; it is used in {ahita zongin}, which means even so or nevertheless.
<a> and <hitakpi> written as one word: that it truly is so, what really is the case
<ahi>, it is, with the question ending {-tam} at the end of a question: is it, could it be; it gives the question a tone of wondering and is often followed by <maw>; compare <aitam>
<ahita> and <zong> written as one word, followed by <in>: at the start of a sentence nevertheless, after a clause although it is so

terms: those who are/the ones that are
definition: The verb <ahi>, be, with the plural <te>, turning the words before it into a noun: {innkuan lutang ahite} is those who are heads of families, {kham ahite} is the things that are of gold.
<a> and <hithei>, can be, written as one word: what is possible; {ahithei zahin} and {ahithei bangin} are as much as possible, as far as one can
man of Giloh, David's counselor, who joined Absalom's revolt
name of several priests, among them the grandson of Eli who was the father of Ahimelek, and the father of Zadok
<a> and <hizaw> written as one word: it is rather so, it is this more than that
The verb <ahi>, be, with <zo>, be able: {ahizo nawn lo} is no longer able to be, and {ahizo zahzahin} is as far as is possible.
<ahi> and <zong> written as one word, mostly followed by <in>: even so, however; begins a sentence that goes against what was just said
<ahi> and <zongin> written as one word, mostly at the start of a sentence: although that is so, but
written abbreviation of <ahihkeileh>, or, placed between two alternatives
written abbreviation of {ahih kei leh}, if it is not so: or, or else
town in the territory of Asher whose people were not driven out
name of two people: a child of Sheshan in the line of Judah, and the parent of Zabad, one of David's warriors
township of the city of Yangon
the largest city of the state of Gujarat in the west of India
son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin, ancestor of the Ahohite clan
ancestor named in {Ahoh-te beh}, the Ahohite clan of Benjamin, to which several of David's warriors belonged
The word <hoih>, good, with the prefix <a>: that which is good, the good one; {ahoih nate} is good things, and {ahoih ahoih lo} is whether good or bad.
<a> and <hoihbek> written as one word: what is just right, the proper amount and no more
<a> and <hoihding> written as one word: it would be good, or what would be good; {ahoihding zahin} is as good as it should be
The word <ahoih>, what is good, with the suffix <in>: in a good way; {ahoihin gamta} is do what is right.
<a> and <hoihlai> written as one word: that which is still good or still in working condition
<a> and <hoihlam> written as one word: the good side of a matter; {ahoihlam in} is in a good way, for good, and {ahoihlam ah} is toward the better
<a> and <hoihlo> written as one word: what is not good, the bad one; {ahoihlo in} is badly
<a> and <hoihloh> written as one word: its being bad, that it is not good; {ahoihloh banah} is besides being bad, {ahoihloh hangin} because it is bad
<a> with <hoihlohna> written as one word: what is not good in something, its bad side or fault, set against <ahoihna>
<a> and <hoihlolam> written as one word: the bad side of a matter; with <in> or <ah>, in a bad way, on the negative side
<a> with <hoihna>, goodness, written as one word: the good in something, its advantage, set against <ahoihlohna> or {a siatna}, its harm
<a> and <hoihpen>, best, written as one word: the best one, or best after a noun
The word <ahoih>, that which is good, with the plural suffix <te>: the good ones; {gamtatna ahoihte} is good deeds.

terms: the best possible/as good as can be
definition: <a> and <hoihthei> written as one word, before <pen> or <penpen>: as good as it can be; {ahoihthei penpen in} is in the best possible way

terms: the best possible/as well as possible
definition: <a>, <hoih>, good, and <theipen>, the most that can be, written as one word: the best that can be, usually with <in>, as well as possible
The word <hoih>, good, with the prefix <a>, <zaw>, more, and the suffix <in>: in a better way, even better than what is named before <sangin>.

terms: for the better/so as to be better
definition: <ahoih> and <zawding> written as one word: what will be better; {ahoihzawding in} is so that it becomes better
<a> and <hon>, open, written as one word: he opens, the opening of
<a> with <hon>, group, written as one word; {ahon in} is as a group, together
<a>, <hon>, rescue, and <ding>, will, written as one word: in order to rescue someone, and {ahonding te} the rescuers
<a>, <hon>, open, and <ding>, will, written as one word: what is still to be opened
<a> and <hong> written as one word before a verb: he, she, it or they, with the particle that turns the action toward the speaker, as in {ahong gen hi}, he told us
<a> and <hongpiang> written as one word: it comes about; {ahongpiang ding} is what is going to happen
<a> and <honhon>, group upon group, written as one word; {ahonhon in} is in groups, many together
<a> and <honkhia> written as one word: he rescues, the one who rescued; {nuntakna ahonkhia} is saved the life of
<a>, <honkhia>, rescue, and <ding>, will, written as one word; {ahonkhiading in} is in order to rescue them
<a> and <honkhiapa> written as one word, placed after the one who was saved: the man who rescued him, her or them
<a> and <honkhiat> written as one word: he or they rescued, or the ones who brought someone out of danger
<ahon> and <leh> written as one word: when he or she opened it, followed by what was found
<a> and <hon>, open, with the ending {-na} written as one word: the thing it is opened with, said of a key
<a> and <honsak> written as one word: he or she opens something for someone, or the one that opens it; {lampi ahonsak} is open the way
<a> and <hontheih> written as one word, before <nading>: so that they can open a shop or a locked thing
<a> and <hopih> written as one word: he speaks to, the one he talks with
<a> and <hot> written as one word, mostly before <khiat>: he rescues, or the one who rescues; {ahot khiatsawm} is he tries to rescue
<a>, he or they, and <hotkhiat>, written as one word: he or they rescue someone, used before words such as <ciangin>, <sawm> and <nop>
<ahotkhiat>, he or they rescue, and <ding>, will or to, written as one word: to rescue someone, that they should rescue
<ahotkhiat>, he or she rescues, and <zia>, manner, written as one word: the way in which he or she rescued someone
spelling of Asherah in 2 Kings 13.6, a Canaanite goddess and the wooden pole set up for her worship
<a> and <hu>, breath, written as one word: his or her breath, breathing; of a thing its vapour, gas or blast
<a> written as one word with a verb meaning shield or protect, a different word from <hu> breath: the one who guards; {a nuntakna ahu ding galkap} is the soldiers who are to guard his life
<a> and <huai> written as one word: a named cut of the slaughtered animal that is shared out by the piece; which part of the carcass is not settled
<a> with <huaisia>, dreadful, written as one word: severe, the worst, said of fires, accidents and disasters
<ahuaisia>, severe, and <diak>, especially, written as one word: the one hit hardest, the most serious case among several
<a>, <huaisia>, dreadful or serious, and <lua>, too much, written as one word; said of injuries, mostly in {ahuaisialua omlo}, there is none that is serious
<a>, <huaisia>, severe, and <pen>, here the mark of the highest degree, written as one word: the most terrible of its kind, said of accidents, fires, storms and attacks
<ahuaisia>, terrible, and <penpen>, the very most, written as one word: the worst of all, said of disasters, fires and accidents
<a>, <huaisia> and the intensifier <pi> written as one word: very serious, said of an injury; {liamna ahuaisiapi omlo} is there is no serious injury
